page: Amazon Web Services r9g.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture using ninth-generation AWS Graviton processors. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores running at a nominal clock frequency of 3.3 GHz, with a single hardware execution thread per core. Memory capacity totals 512.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a uniform allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU without hardware multi-threading contention.

Network infrastructure for r9g.16xlarge delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 34 Gbps. The instance provides no bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent data volumes, operating system filesystems, and working caches require network-attached storage provisioned via AWS Elastic Block Store. No dedicated GPU accelerators are attached to this configuration, focusing resource utilization solely on general-purpose ARM computation and memory-centric operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the Graviton processor design provides high density and power-efficient ARM compute per core alongside a large memory pool, offering favorable operational efficiency relative to legacy x86 architectures. Tradeoffs include the requirement for ARM64 software binary compatibility and reliance on remote network-attached volumes for I/O operations due to the complete absence of local disk drives.

Amazon Web Services r9g.16xlarge is engineered for large-scale memory-bound applications, including in-memory key-value databases, distributed caching systems, large transactional relational databases, real-time analytics pipelines, and data-intensive batch processing workloads.
